reviewNote: v2.0.0 sample set. Facts checked on 2026-11-17 against the sources named on each question and object (AI-assisted build); answers with a `fact` reference are derived from geo-objects.json by the validator. A human spot-check is recommended before wide release.

questions.text: Select every country the Alps cross.
questions.description: Two tiny Alpine countries are too small for this map. You only need the ones you can tap.
questions.explanation: The Alps stretch about 1,200 km across France, Switzerland, Italy, Germany, Austria and Slovenia, plus Monaco and Liechtenstein, which are too small for this map.

questions.text: Select every country the Andes run through.
questions.explanation: The Andes run through seven countries: Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile and Argentina.

questions.text: Select the three countries crossed by the Atlas Mountains.
questions.explanation: The Atlas Mountains stretch about 2,500 km through Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia, separating the Sahara from the Mediterranean and the Atlantic.

questions.text: Tap the country where Mount Kilimanjaro stands.
questions.explanation: Kilimanjaro, 5,895 m, is in Tanzania. It is the highest volcano in the Eastern Hemisphere.

questions.text: True or false: Mount Kilimanjaro is a volcano.
questions.explanation: True. Kilimanjaro is a large dormant stratovolcano in Tanzania.

questions.text: Which mountain range contains Mount Everest?
questions.explanation: Everest is in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas. At 8,849 m it is the highest mountain on Earth.

questions.text: The border between which two countries runs over the summit of Mount Everest?
questions.explanation: Everest's summit marks part of the border between Nepal and China.

questions.text: Mont Blanc, the highest mountain of the Alps, lies on the border of which two countries?
questions.explanation: The Mont Blanc massif lies on the border of France and Italy. At about 4,807 m it is the highest mountain in Europe outside the Caucasus.

questions.text: Aconcagua is the highest mountain outside Asia. Tap the country where it is.
questions.explanation: Aconcagua is in Mendoza Province, Argentina, in the Andes.

questions.text: Mount Elbrus is the highest peak of which mountain range?
questions.explanation: Elbrus, 5,642 m, in southern Russia, is the highest peak of the Caucasus Mountains.

questions.text: Match each mountain with its mountain range.
questions.explanation: Everest is in the Himalayas, Mont Blanc in the Alps, Aconcagua in the Andes and Elbrus in the Caucasus.

questions.text: The Khyber Pass crosses the border between which two countries?
questions.explanation: The Khyber Pass is in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, along the border with Afghanistan.

questions.text: Which mountain pass is marked on the map?
questions.explanation: That is the Khyber Pass, between Pakistan and Afghanistan. The other three passes are in the Alps.

questions.text: The Brenner Pass over the Alps forms the border between which two countries?
questions.explanation: The Brenner Pass forms the border between Austria and Italy.

questions.text: Which volcano is marked on the map?
questions.explanation: That is Mount Fuji, an active stratovolcano on Honshu and Japan's highest mountain at 3,776 m.

questions.text: Mount Vesuvius destroyed the Roman city of Pompeii in 79 AD. Tap the country where it stands.
questions.explanation: Vesuvius stands near Naples, in southern Italy.

questions.text: True or false: Mount Etna is an active volcano on the island of Sicily.
questions.explanation: True. Etna is an active stratovolcano on the east coast of Sicily, Italy.

questions.text: Which river carved the Grand Canyon?
questions.explanation: The Colorado River carved the Grand Canyon in Arizona, exposing nearly two billion years of rock layers.

questions.text: The Gotthard Base Tunnel, the world's longest railway tunnel, runs under the Alps in which country? Tap it.
questions.explanation: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is in Switzerland. It is the world's longest railway tunnel and the first flat, low-level route through the Alps.

questions.text: Tap the country where the Kathmandu Valley lies.
questions.explanation: The bowl-shaped Kathmandu Valley lies in the Himalayas of Nepal and is home to the capital, Kathmandu.
